commit.message:
docs: refresh README with verified content, structure, and examples

- Rewrites the README onto the standard Aspose FOSS presentation template:
  badge row + banner, a Navigation TOC, an At-a-Glance capability diagram,
  Key Capabilities, Installation, a dedicated Dependencies section, Quick
  Start, and a curated Additional Examples set.
- Adds a module-grouped API Reference table (mirroring the structure of the
  full generated reference documentation) plus a curated set of core/internal
  classes and enumerations, collapsed behind a <details> disclosure so the
  page stays scannable.
- Adds a Documentation & Resources section linking the real getting-started
  guide, how-to/FAQ articles, full API reference, and the issue tracker.
- Adds a Scope and Limitations section naming the real, verified constraints
  (no barcode decoding, PDF rendering not implemented, ECI/GS1 fields present
  in the options surface but not yet implemented) and a single, standalone
  Enterprise Edition paragraph for readers who need PDF rendering or
  additional symbologies.
- Adds Development and Testing instructions and a standard MIT License
  section linking the real license file.

Verification: every code example was checked against the real, current
package surface; every claim in Scope and Limitations was verified against
source; the diagram and API Reference detail were checked with this
project's own automated structural/content gates before this change was
proposed.

Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

repo.description: Open-source pure Python library for generating Code 128, Code 39, EAN, QR Code, and UPC barcodes in SVG or PNG, with simple pip installation and no native dependencies.
repo.name: Aspose.BarCode-FOSS-for-Python
